extraction_scope: Worker-6 bounded mechanism adjudication from source text and figures; direct mechanism claims are limited to membrane morphology/time-kill/salt-sensitivity evidence actually assayed in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LS-AMP-F1 caused visible S. albus surface damage in SEM after 10 and 30 min and reduced E. coli colony counts in time-kill assays at 2x and 5x MIC; this supports rapid membrane-disruptive antibacterial action for LS-AMP-F1.
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM/time-kill assays were shown for selected representative strains and should not be generalized to every tested clinical isolate.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:3.5. The Rapid Antimicrobial Activities and Mechanisms of LS-AMPs

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Mg2+ reduced antibacterial activity of LS-AMP-E1 and LS-AMP-F1 against E. coli, supporting a membrane/cation competition interpretation rather than a precise molecular target.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The salt assay supports membrane-affinity context but does not identify a specific receptor or intracellular target.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:3.5. The Rapid Antimicrobial Activities and Mechanisms of LS-AMPs

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LS-AMP-E1 and LS-AMP-F1 inhibited E. coli biofilm formation at MIC and sub-MIC concentrations; this is an antibiofilm phenotype, not a resolved biofilm molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Crystal-violet biomass reduction does not identify the molecular route of biofilm inhibition.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=16:3.3. The Anti-Biofilm Effects of LS-AMPs

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LS-AMP-E1 and LS-AMP-F1 potentiated selected antibiotic combinations by checkerboard/FICI assays; this is a synergy phenotype and does not prove a single shared drug-resistance mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Checkerboard assays support interaction strength but not a molecular mechanism of antibiotic potentiation.
